title: Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0001-p1】Efficient delivery of plasmid DNA (pDNA) to the nucleus is a major hurdle for clinical gene therapy and DNA vaccines. In post-mitotic or slowly dividing tissues such as muscle, skin and dendritic cells the nuclear envelope remains intact, so pDNA can enter only through nuclear pore complexes (NPCs) or during infrequent mitosis, and only ~1–5% of administered non-viral DNA is estimated to reach the nucleus (Yao et al. 2013). Microinjection studies established the consequence directly: DNA retained in the cytoplasm gives virtually no expression, whereas nuclear injection yields expression in the majority of cells (Dean et al. 2005). Nuclear import is therefore the rate-limiting step for most therapeutically relevant, non-dividing targets (Munkonge et al. 2003). In practice, this leads to high doses, variable responses and transient expression: the ZyCoV-D DNA vaccine required three intradermal doses of 2 mg to achieve ~66% efficacy (Khobragade et al. 2022), responses are dose-dependent and variable (Dean 1997), and because plasmids remain episomal their expression is diluted in proliferating cells and may require re-dosing. Electroporation-enhanced DNA vaccines achieve ~100-1000x higher antigen expression than naked DNA, illustrating how strongly outcome tracks with the efficiency of nuclear access (Sardesai and Weiner 2011). A major determinant is the cell cycle: dividing cells transiently lose the envelope and admit even large plasmids passively, whereas quiescent tissues such as neurons and cardiomyocytes depend entirely on active transport, which is one reason intramuscular DNA vaccines are less immunogenic in large animals than in rodents (Liu 2011; Yao et al. 2013).

【Introduction · s0001-p2】Efforts to enhance nuclear entry must also be considered in relation to platform safety. Plasmids are designed to remain extrachromosomal, and regulatory expectations are that integration occurs at a rate far below the spontaneous mutation rate (U.S. Food and Drug Administration. 2007; Martinez-Puente et al. 2022); no integration-related adverse events have been attributed to DNA vaccines or therapies, although electroporation modestly increases integration risk and insertional mutagenesis remains a low-probability hazard for plasmid platforms (Ledwith et al. 2000). Unmethylated CpG motifs and cytosolic double-stranded DNA also engage innate sensors such as endosomal TLR9 and cytosolic cGAS-STING; this is advantageous for vaccines but can produce local or systemic inflammation, and delivery methods that raise the cytosolic DNA load amplify the effect. pDNA elicits little anti-vector immunity compared with viral vectors, which is a regulatory advantage (Kay 2011), but repeated dosing, carrier immunogenicity and the tissue injury caused by physical delivery methods all remain regulatory considerations (Sardesai and Weiner 2011; Martinez-Puente et al. 2022).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Engineered, multivalent and screening-derived designs · s0002-s2004-p1】Recent work has moved from using natural NLSs toward engineering and screening motifs for delivery performance. Multivalency is the simplest lever: tandem cNLS repeats and hybrid uptake/targeting constructs such as TAT-SV40 (YGRKKRRQRRRP-KKKRKV) increase local basic charge density, improve nucleic-acid condensation and combine distinct trafficking functions. Yi et al. reported an approximately 200-fold increase in luciferase expression when an SV40-type NLS was added to a TAT-based carrier; heterodimeric TAT-NLS systems outperformed the corresponding monofunctional peptides, and a lipopeptide TAT-NLS formulation yielded compact, homogeneous and storage-stable DNA nanoparticles (Yi et al. 2012; Doh 2015; Pambudi et al. 2024). Because the CPP component contributes chiefly to uptake and cytosolic access rather than to receptor-mediated import, these systems follow mixed intracellular itineraries and their gains should not be attributed to nuclear targeting alone.

【Engineered, multivalent and screening-derived designs · s0002-s2004-p2】This caveat applies with particular force to CPP-derived motifs themselves. HIV Tat (YGRKKRRQRRR) accumulates in the nucleus and is often grouped with NLSs, but Tat-mediated nuclear entry is relatively insensitive to wheat germ agglutinin, does not display the ATP dependence of classical import, and can carry cargo larger than 90 nm, well beyond what cNLS-driven import accommodates (Vives et al. 1997; Nitin et al. 2009). Arginine-rich viral motifs can nonetheless be recognised directly by importin-β (Palmeri and Malim 1999; Truant and Cullen 1999), which places this class in a mechanistic grey zone between membrane translocation and receptor-mediated transport. Tat-like peptides may therefore enable nuclear entry of unusually large assemblies while offering less mechanistic interpretability than classical cNLS motifs.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · s0010-p1】Nuclear delivery of plasmid DNA remains a fundamental bottleneck in nonviral gene therapy, particularly in post-mitotic and quiescent cells where the nuclear envelope is a permanent barrier to passive entry. The two strategies developed to overcome it operate on distinct principles. NLS peptides, which include classical monopartite and bipartite motifs together with their engineered, histone-derived and CPP-hybrid variants, recruit the importin-α/β machinery directly to the DNA cargo. DTS elements instead recruit endogenous NLS-bearing transcription factors to specific plasmid sequences, achieving piggyback import that is most powerful in non-dividing cells and that can confer cell-type specificity when lineage-restricted factors are engaged. Both depend critically on the carrier in which they are deployed: over-condensation occludes the signal, whereas insufficient protection allows cytoplasmic degradation before import can occur.

【Conclusion · s0010-p2】Despite this mechanistic evidence, neither strategy has been incorporated as a declared core mechanism in any approved nonviral product. Clinical programmes have relied instead on electroporation, receptor-mediated endocytosis and local high-dose administration. All of these raise cytosolic DNA availability without engaging the import machinery directly. Bridging this gap requires a framework that treats cell division status, carrier-DNA accessibility and intracellular signalling context together. The Nuclear Accessibility Index does so, and applied as an axis vector rather than as a single sum it partitions the design space into regions with qualitatively different recommendations, as set out in Section 9.6.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · f0001】Figure 1. Mechanistic pathways of NLS-mediated nuclear delivery of plasmid DNA. Various nuclear localisation signal (NLS) platforms facilitate plasmid DNA transport into the nucleus through distinct receptor usage and nuclear trafficking mechanisms. In the classical importin α/β pathway, monopartite or bipartite basic NLS motifs, such as the SV40 T-antigen NLS and nucleoplasmin-derived NLS, are recognised by importin α, which subsequently recruits importin β to mediate docking and translocation through the nuclear pore complex (NPC). In contrast, non-classical pathways utilise alternative nuclear transport receptors, including direct importin-β binding or transportin-mediated import, as exemplified by IGFBP3-derived motifs and the hnRNP A1 M9 domain. Histone-derived NLS systems employ importin-4-dependent trafficking of histone H3/H4 tail motifs and additionally promote chromatin-associated nuclear retention after NPC translocation. Auxiliary trafficking mechanisms, including CPP-mediated intracellular uptake, endosomal escape, microtubule-dependent transport, and NPC docking factors, may further enhance nuclear accumulation of plasmid DNA. Collectively, these pathways demonstrate that NLS-mediated plasmid delivery involves multiple mechanistically distinct strategies that improve nuclear import efficiency and transgene expression.

【Figure 2. · f0002】Figure 2. General mechanism of DTS-mediated nuclear transport. (1) Transcription factors (TFs) in the cytoplasm recognise and bind to DNA targeting sequences (DTS) on the plasmid DNA. (2) The nuclear localisation signals (NLSs) of the bound TFs become exposed and coat the plasmid DNA. (3) Importin α/β recognises the NLSs and associates with the TF–DNA complex to form an import complex. (4) The complex translocates through the nuclear pore complex (NPC). (5) In the nucleus, the plasmid DNA is released from the import machinery and becomes available for transcription by RNA polymerase II. Abbreviations: DTS, DNA targeting sequence; TF, transcription factor; NLS, nuclear localisation signal; NPC, nuclear pore complex; RNA Pol II, RNA polymerase II.

【Figure 3. · f0003】Figure 3. Chemical strategies for DNA and peptide binding.

sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《Overcoming the nuclear barrier in nonviral gene therapy: mechanisms, carrier design, and translational perspectives on NLS peptide and DNA targeting sequence strategies》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【Axis II—carrier–DNA accessibility · s0009-s2003-p1】Nuclear targeting mechanisms, whether NLS-peptide–based or DTS-based, share a common prerequisite: the plasmid must be present in the cytosol in a form that is accessible to the relevant import machinery. This prerequisite is frequently overlooked when NLS or DTS strategies are evaluated in isolation from their carrier context. For NLS-mediated import, the NLS motif must be physically accessible to importin-α/β receptors; steric occlusion of the NLS within a highly condensed polyplex can abolish importin binding even when the peptide is covalently attached to the DNA (Ciolina et al. 1999; Skowicki et al. 2024). For DTS-mediated import, the binding sites must be accessible to cytoplasmic transcription factors, a condition that is similarly compromised when plasmid DNA is over-condensed by a cationic carrier at high N/P ratios (Lam and Dean 2010; Bai et al. 2017). Conversely, under-protected DNA, delivered with insufficient carrier or after premature complex dissociation, faces rapid cytoplasmic degradation by DNase II and other nucleases, reducing the available substrate for nuclear import (Bai et al. 2017).

【Axis II—carrier–DNA accessibility · s0009-s2003-p2】Axis II therefore captures the balance between protection and accessibility. Over-condensed complexes (e.g. PEI at excessive N/P ratios, over-cationic peptiplexes) = 1 (transcription factor and importin access both impaired; DTS nonfunctional; NLS sterically masked); under-protected or prematurely dissociated complexes = 2 (DNA accessible but cytosolic half-life severely shortened; import window reduced); optimally formulated carriers = 3 (sufficient condensation for nuclease protection, sufficient DNA accessibility for importin and transcription factor recruitment; both NLS and DTS pathways can operate) (Ciolina et al. 1999; Bai et al. 2017; Skowicki et al. 2024).
